tagline: A pine-forest loop through Arizona's high lake country.
intro: The loop sets out in the pines near McNary, on the Fort Apache Indian Reservation, and runs east on Highway 260 to Eagar at the foot of the White Mountains. From there Highway 261 winds south through the forest to Big Lake, at 9,000 feet below Mount Baldy. Highway 273 brings it back north past White Mountain Reservoir and along Sunrise Lake, by the turn for the ski slopes the White Mountain Apache Tribe runs. Part of that stretch was gravel once.
The Highway 260 stretch goes back to the 1870s, when a wagon road brought hay and goods to Fort Apache from Cluff Cienega, now McNary, and from Springerville.

moments.title: McNary
moments.text: In 1924 a lumber company moved its whole operation here from McNary, Louisiana, hundreds of workers included, and brought the town's name along. The mill closed after a fire in 1979.

moments.title: Eagar
moments.text: The first postmistress wanted to call the place Union. The postmaster general said the name was too common, and later trimmed her second choice, Eagarville, to Eagar.

moments.title: Greer
moments.text: Up a 4.6-mile spur, the highest town in Arizona sits at about 8,400 feet with the Little Colorado River running through the middle of it.

practical: Roads to Big Lake close for snow in winter, generally December to early April.
